newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee recovers after RBI makes enquiries.
newsitem.headline: India rupee recovers after RBI makes enquiries.

text.p: The Indian rupee recovered to 35.92/94 against the dollar on Monday after touching a low of 35.94/97 earlier in the day, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 35.91/93 on Monday compared to the previous close of 35.89/90.
There were deals upto 35.95 on Monday, dealers said.
Dealers said there was mild panic dollar buying early in the morning on political worries stemming from Congress Party's decision to withdraw support to the ruling United Front government.
"The RBI called up to check for our views," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. RBI called up several banks but did not intervene, dealers said.
One dealer said a leading Calcutta-based bank also began giving narrow quotes as though to restrain the market.
"RBI has been the only dollar buyer in recent weeks," said a dealer. "I don't expect them to buy today."

He said importers would determine the next course of action. If importers began buying dollars it may weaken the rupee and exporters may then hold on to their dollar proceeds, hoping for further depreciation.
"Right now it does not look like things are going that way," said another dealer.
